vision.why.open: Why did the model say this? Its evidence first, then heatmaps
vision.why.title: Why? {name}
vision.why.subtitle: The model's own evidence first; post-hoc maps under Advanced, with their caveats.
vision.why.loading: Fitting the run's model again on its training images
vision.why.noRunHint: Train a model in the Model tab: "Why?" then shows what it says about this image and the training images it compares it with.
vision.why.evidenceTip: These comparisons are made in the space the model itself reads, so they are part of how it decides, not a story told afterwards (Rudin, 2019). A prediction whose nearest training images disagree with it deserves a second look.
vision.why.stripLabel: The image and its evidence, side by side
vision.why.pickEvidence: Compare with: the nearest training images, then the closest prototype of the predicted class
vision.why.pickNormals: Compare with: the most similar normal training images (their mean distance is the score)
vision.why.loadingOwnMap: Rebuilding each patch from the normal patches
vision.why.ownMap: This map is the model's own computation (its score is read from it), not a post-hoc explanation.
vision.why.advancedHint: counterfactual example, occlusion, Grad-CAM, attention rollout
vision.why.warning: This heatmap is a post-hoc explanation: it shows where the model's output is sensitive, not the reasoning it used. Maps can look plausible even for a model that has learned nothing (Adebayo et al., 2018). For decisions that matter, prefer the nearest examples and prototypes, which are the model's own evidence (Rudin, 2019).
vision.why.cached: Read from the run's cache (computed in {seconds} s).
vision.why.computed: Computed in {seconds} s, kept with the run.
vision.why.moreHint: saliency, SmoothGrad, Integrated Gradients, sanity test
vision.why.costlyIntro: Gradient maps that cost more passes of the network. Each is computed only when you choose it.
vision.why.shownAbove: The map is shown above, under the post-hoc heatmaps.
vision.why.sanityTip: Adebayo et al. (2018): a map that hardly changes when the model's weights are replaced by random ones explains the image, not the model.
vision.why.sanityIntro: The map is computed again with a random head, then with the last blocks of the network made random one after the other. A trustworthy map changes.
vision.why.loadingSanity: Randomising the weights, block by block
vision.why.patchcoreIntro: PatchCore compares every patch of the image with a memory of patches from the normal images. Its score is the most unusual patch; the normal patch closest to it is shown beside it.
vision.why.loadingPatchcore: Building PatchCore's memory of normal patches
vision.why.strip.hint: One zoom for all: Ctrl + wheel or pinch, drag to pan, double click, + − 0
vision.explain.noRunHint: Train a model in the Model tab: this tab then shows the images it holds as typical of each class, the ones it represents worst, and, for a classic model, what it reads in an image.
vision.explain.intro: What the model reads across the whole set. Click any image, here or in the gallery, to see why the model reads it as it does.
vision.explain.loading: Finding the prototypes of each class
vision.explain.prototypesTip: Prototypes are the medoids of each class in the model's space (k-medoids): real images that stand for many others. Criticisms are the images those prototypes represent worst (MMD-critic, Kim et al., 2016): look at them for mislabels, rare kinds or a part of the class the model may not know.
vision.explain.noCritics: None: the prototypes cover the class.
vision.explain.familiesTip: Permutation importance: each family of descriptors is shuffled across the test images, and the drop in balanced accuracy says how much the classic logistic model needs it. Shuffling is done 5 times; the ± is their spread.
